subject: Patrick Clerkin City Council Candidacy
overview: Hosts Danielle Balocca and Chelli Keshavan interviewed City Council candidate Patrick Clerkin regarding his background as a mechanical engineer and his vision for Medford. Clerkin proposed a platform centered on political mediation, housing balance, and enhanced transparency through digital mapping.

items.title: Candidate Introduction and Professional Background
items.summary: Patrick Clerkin introduced himself as a seven-year Medford resident and mechanical engineer running for City Council.

items.title: Political Philosophy and Mediation
items.summary: Clerkin presented his "bridge" campaign theme, emphasizing his goal to act as a mediator between polarized political groups to find common ground.

items.title: Local Policy Priorities
items.summary: The candidate identified the balance between homeowners and tenants and the need for improved government transparency as his primary concerns.

items.title: Handling Social and Cultural Controversies
items.summary: Regarding divisive topics like school renaming, Clerkin advocated for providing fuller context and respectful dialogue to reduce community animosity.

items.title: Transparency and Communication Initiatives
items.summary: Clerkin proposed improving city governance through digital mapping of department projects and hosting regular updates for constituents.

items.title: Equity and Institutional Access
items.summary: The candidate discussed his approach to equity, focusing on broad information access and neutrality while acknowledging the historical exclusion of marginalized groups from City Hall.

items.title: Personal Background and Campaign Announcements
items.summary: Clerkin concluded the interview by sharing personal background details and announcing a campaign fundraiser at Ford Tavern.
